answer: Coordinated Action Pricing makes each independent identity's action raise a shared cost curve keyed to correlate timing, so a sybil cluster pays a steep premium while lone actors stay near the baseline; the curve is the shale that absorbs scattered pressure without fracturing. A cheap signal of distinctness—randomized submission offsets—compounds, because clones marching in lockstep multiply the price. The attacker's bill scales with cluster size squared, and each extra identity must fund its own growing share, turning a swarm into a costly oasis of uniformity.
